updates.name: Back out of the home internet address eligibility screen and land back on IMEI validation
updates.custom_requirements:
## What this test is about
As a Metro by T-Mobile authorized dealer, I want Back on the home internet address screen to put me back at the point where I enter the device's serial number, so that when a customer changes their mind before giving an address I can start the line over cleanly instead of being stranded mid-sale.

Some background. Metro sells home internet as a small box (a "gateway") the customer takes home, which turns the Metro 5G signal into home Wi-Fi. Because the box only works at one address, selling one puts the rep through two extra screens a phone sale never sees: a screen where the customer's street address is checked for coverage, and a screen where both the customer and the rep have to sign off that the box will only be used at that address. A rep in a store backs out of these all the time — the customer is not sure of the address, or decides against home internet once they hear the terms.

This test covers the FIRST of those two screens only — the address screen. Back there must take the rep back to the serial-number screen and leave nothing behind: the line being built is dropped, the same gateway can be entered again straight away, and the address form comes up blank the second time. Backing out of the acknowledgement screen is a separate test.

This test starts from nothing: it opens a new account and activates a phone as line 1 first, because home internet can never be a customer's first line, and only then starts the gateway on line 2.

## Related tickets
RTPL-2289 (home internet screens and Back behaviour), RTPL-2008 (Home internet epic)

## Preconditions
- Nothing pre-existing is needed — this test builds its own account from scratch. Home internet cannot be the first line on an account, so the phone is activated first as line 1 and the home internet gateway is added afterwards as line 2.
- The store is set up to sell home internet. If the home internet screens never appear for a gateway serial number, stop and contact the manual QA team before going further — the feature is switched off for the environment, not broken.

## Test data
- **New customer details:** Any test customer: a first name, a last name, a unique email address per run, and a street address with its zip code (for example 405 LEXINGTON AVE, 10174, NEW YORK, NY)  _(verified: QA / UAT3 2026-09-04 — the Account information screen was read live and asks only for First name, Middle initial, Last name, Email, Address, Address 2, Zip code, City and State)_
- **Customer phone number for the identity check:** 2125551234  _(verified: QA / UAT3 — this number has passed the identity check in previous activation runs on this environment)_
- **Phone for line 1 (IMEI):** The next unused phone IMEI from the RTGO Data workbook  _(verified: RTGO Data workbook, UAT3 sheet — the workbook's Used column is unreliable, so take the first IMEI the app actually accepts. Which phone it is does not matter to this test)_
- **SIM card for line 1:** The next unused physical SIM card number from the RTGO Data workbook  _(verified: RTGO Data workbook, UAT3 sheet — same caveat; if a SIM is rejected, move to the next row)_
- **Home internet gateway IMEI (the gateway's serial number):** 999977129737997  _(verified: UAT3 2026-07-29 — this serial number was accepted as a home internet device and opened the home internet screens)_

## Automation Notes
- The point of this test is WHERE the rep lands after Back on the address screen: the "IMEI validation" screen, with the home internet line gone from the cart. Assert both the screen and the cart — a line left behind in the cart is the other way this can go wrong.
- If the gateway serial number is refused, or the home internet screens never appear, try the next candidate serial number from the RTGO Data workbook first. If none work, contact the manual QA team to get a working home internet gateway serial number — do not sit blocked and do not go hunting for data alone.
- The account and the phone line are built by this test, not assumed. If the phone IMEI or the SIM is rejected, take the next row from the RTGO Data workbook; if the whole pool is exhausted, contact the manual QA team for working device data rather than sitting blocked.
- CONFIRM BEFORE AUTOMATING: the account screens were re-read live on 2026-09-04 only as far as "Account information" — the environment refused to create the account past that point that day. Confirm the identity-check screen and the phone-line steps on the first run and correct this ticket if the app asks for anything else.

steps.expected: The rep is signed in and the store dashboard is shown.

steps.action: Start a new account for a new customer.
steps.expected: The "Account information" screen is shown, asking for the customer's name, email and address.

steps.action: Fill in the new customer's details — first name, last name, email, street address, zip code, city and state — and select Continue.
steps.expected: The details are accepted and the "ID verification" screen is shown. Use a different email address on every run; the app rejects an email that is already on another account.

steps.action: Enter the customer's phone number for the identity check and select Continue.
steps.expected: The identity check passes and the "IMEI validation" screen is shown for the customer's first line.

steps.action: Type the phone's serial number into the IMEI field and select Continue. This phone becomes line 1.
steps.expected: The phone is accepted and the "SIM validation" screen is shown.

steps.action: Enter the SIM card number for the phone and select Continue.
steps.expected: The SIM is accepted and the "Phone number selection" screen is shown.

steps.action: Choose one of the offered phone numbers for the phone line and select Continue.
steps.expected: The chosen number is attached to line 1 and the "Protection selection" screen is shown.

steps.action: On "Protection selection", select Skip and confirm the decline when asked.
steps.expected: No device protection is added to the phone line and the "Plan selection" screen is shown.

steps.action: Choose the offered phone plan and select Continue.
steps.expected: The plan and its monthly charge are shown against line 1 in the cart, and the "Promotion selection" screen is shown.

steps.action: On "Promotion selection", decline the promotions for the phone line and confirm when asked.
steps.expected: No promotion is added to the phone line and the "Add on services" screen is shown.

steps.action: On "Add on services", select Skip for the phone line.
steps.expected: No add-on is added to the phone line and the rep is offered Create subscriber.

steps.action: Select Create subscriber and confirm it in the panel that opens.
steps.expected: A "Subscriber created" confirmation is shown for the phone line — line 1 is now active — offering to add another line or to continue to the order summary.

steps.action: Select "Add another line" to start line 2.
steps.expected: The "IMEI validation" screen is shown again, this time for line 2. The activated phone line stays in the cart.

steps.action: Type the home internet gateway's serial number into the IMEI field and select Continue.
steps.expected: A panel titled "Confirm home internet device" opens and reads: "The IMEI entered is a home internet device and requires extra details to activate. Click continue to proceed with activating this home internet device."

steps.action: Select Continue on the "Confirm home internet device" panel.
steps.expected: The "Home internet address eligibility" screen is shown with an empty address form and Back and Continue at the bottom.

steps.action: Select Back on the "Home internet address eligibility" screen.
steps.expected: The rep is taken back to the "IMEI validation" screen. The home internet line that was being built is dropped — it is no longer in the cart, and no home internet step is left showing anywhere in the flow.

steps.action: Type the same home internet gateway serial number into the IMEI field again and select Continue.
steps.expected: The serial number is accepted again — backing out did not lock it up — and the "Confirm home internet device" panel opens as it did the first time.

steps.action: Select Continue on the "Confirm home internet device" panel.
steps.expected: The "Home internet address eligibility" screen opens with every field empty. Nothing is carried over from the line that was backed out of.

steps.action: Stop here. Do NOT submit any payment.
steps.expected: The order is left with only the phone line activated earlier in this test on it, and the gateway's serial number is left unused so the same one can be used again on the next run.
